raw_case_text:
Mrs. OB was a 32-year-old G4P3+0  (3 alive) trader who presented on the 5th of March, 2013, in the gynaecological emergency room with abdominal pain of 4 days' duration and bleeding per vaginam of 2 days' duration following 8 weeks of amenorrhea.
Examination revealed that she was pale and dehydrated with a respiratory rate of 28 excursions per minute, pulse rate was 104 beats per minute, and blood pressure was 134/74 mmHg. There was generalized abdominal tenderness; pelvic examination revealed cervical os that was closed, with tenderness in the fornices, and the pouch of Douglas was full. The uterine size could not be assessed because of tenderness.
A clinical impression of suspected ruptured tubal gestation was made; urine pregnancy test was positive. Packed cell volume was 18%. Urgent abdominopelvic ultrasound scanning revealed bulky uterus measuring 11.37 x 4.83 cm in its longitudinal and transverse diameters. It showed normal myometrial echogenicity. There was a decidual reaction within the endometrium. A large mixed echogenic structure with irregular and ill-defined margins was seen in the right adnexum suggestive of ruptured ectopic gestation with surrounding hematoma. There was gross increase in intraperitoneal fluid suggestive of haemoperitoneum.
The patient was resuscitated with intravenous fluids and informed consent for exploratory laparotomy was obtained. Intraoperative findings included 2.7 litres of haemoperitoneum, ruptured right tubal ampullary gestation, and bulbous fatty mass at the fimbrial portion of the left tube measuring 4 cm x 6 cm, and the uterus was bulky. At laparotomy she had bilateral salpingectomy.
The patient was transfused with 3 units of whole blood. The posttransfusion packed cell volume was 25%. She made significant improvement and she was discharged home on the 7th postoperative day.
She was seen in gynaecological clinic 2 weeks later with histology report of specimens which revealed left and right fallopian tubes showing distension of the lamina by chorionic villi of varying sizes, hemorrhage, and decidualized stroma. Also seen are multiple granulomas with calcified ova of S. haematobium with their characteristic terminal spines, features consistent with bilateral ectopic gestation with Schistosoma induced salpingitis. She was comanaged with a parasitologist. She, however, declined urine and stool microscopy before using oral praziquantel (20 mg/kg twice a day for one day), after which urine and stool microscopy for ova of parasites done a month after medication was negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old gravida 4, para 3+0 woman presented to the gynecological emergency room with a 4-day history of abdominal pain and 2 days of vaginal bleeding following 8 weeks of amenorrhea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Following an 8-week period of amenorrhea, the patient developed generalized abdominal pain lasting 4 days accompanied by vaginal bleeding for 2 days prior to emergency presentation on March 5, 2013.
subjective.past_medical_history: Gravida 4, para 3+0 (3 living children); worked as a trader in Nigeria.

objective.physical_examination: Pale and dehydrated with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths/min, pulse rate of 104 bpm, and blood pressure of 134/74 mmHg. Abdominal examination showed generalized tenderness; pelvic examination revealed a closed cervical os, bilateral forniceal tenderness, and a full pouch of Douglas (uterine size was unassessable due to tenderness).
objective.routine_investigations: Urine pregnancy test was positive, and packed cell volume (PCV) was 18% (increasing to 25% after transfusion of 3 units of whole blood). Urgent abdominopelvic ultrasound showed a bulky uterus (11.37 x 4.83 cm) with normal myometrial echogenicity and endometrial decidual reaction, a large irregular mixed-echogenic right adnexal mass with surrounding hematoma, and gross hemoperitoneum.
objective.advanced_workup: Exploratory laparotomy revealed 2.7 L of hemoperitoneum, a ruptured right tubal ampullary ectopic gestation, a 4 x 6 cm bulbous fatty mass at the fimbrial end of the left fallopian tube, and a bulky uterus; bilateral salpingectomy was performed. Histopathology of both left and right fallopian tubes demonstrated luminal distension by chorionic villi of varying sizes, hemorrhage, decidualized stroma, and multiple granulomas containing calcified Schistosoma haematobium ova with characteristic terminal spines.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed bilateral tubal ectopic gestation secondary to Schistosoma haematobium-induced granulomatous salpingitis on bilateral fallopian tube histopathology. Following resuscitation, bilateral salpingectomy, and transfusion of 3 units of whole blood, she was discharged on postoperative day 7 and subsequently treated with oral praziquantel 20 mg/kg twice daily for 1 day; follow-up urine and stool microscopy 1 month post-treatment were negative for parasite ova.
